summary_html: Agency **files a court petition** to open a **dependency** (or similar) case. Federal funding frameworks (IV-E/ASFA) link court oversight, reasonable-efforts findings, and permanency timelines to downstream actions.
authority_html:

provisions_triggered.name: Due Process / Law of the Land

case_law.method: v1.1.0 case-law rebuild: authorities selected per decision point, each opinion retrieved from CourtListener and read; holding and quote taken from the opinion text; independently re-verified before release. Previous keyword-matched Justia listings were removed.

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Department of Children & Families v. A.L.
key_cases.holding: The Court reversed an abuse-or-neglect finding based on prenatal cocaine use, holding Title 9 requires competent proof of actual harm to the child or of imminent danger or substantial risk of harm.
key_cases.relevance: A.L. defines the proofs the Division must be able to present before it files and litigates a Title 9 complaint.
key_cases.quote: If an expectant mother's drug use causes actual harm to the physical, mental, or emotional condition of a newborn child, a finding of abuse or neglect is appropriate.

key_cases.case_name: Division of Youth & Family Services v. G.M.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that after a Title 9 abuse-or-neglect finding the parent is entitled to a dispositional hearing on whether the children may safely be returned, and remanded because none was held.
key_cases.relevance: G.M. maps the statutory sequence a petition sets in motion, from fact-finding to disposition.
key_cases.quote: upon a finding of abuse and neglect, the offending parent or guardian is entitled to a dispositional hearing

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Department of Children & Families v. I.S.
key_cases.holding: The Court held that a Title 9 action must be dismissed when no abuse or neglect is proved, but that jurisdiction may continue where the Division also proceeds under Title 30 to secure needed services for the child.
key_cases.relevance: I.S. tells the Division which statutory authority its petition must invoke for the relief it seeks.
key_cases.quote: when the Division brings its complaint also under the authority granted to it under Title 30, the court's jurisdiction may continue

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. C.H.
key_cases.court: New Jersey Superior Court, Appellate Division
key_cases.holding: The court held the trial judge's sua sponte dismissal of the abuse-or-neglect complaint mid-hearing violated due process and remanded, while affirming the dismissal that followed a noticed motion.
key_cases.relevance: C.H. protects the Division's right to present its full case once a petition is filed.
key_cases.quote: the court's sua sponte dismissal of the abuse or neglect complaint against C.H. was a due process violation necessitating a remand

key_cases.case_name: New Jersey Division of Youth & Family Services v. A.R.G.
key_cases.holding: The Court affirmed as modified and remanded for de novo reconsideration, holding that 'aggravated circumstances' excusing the Division from reasonable reunification efforts under N.J.S.A. 30:4C-11.3 is a fact-specific inquiry and that a parent must first receive notice of the underlying facts and theory the State will rely on.
key_cases.relevance: A.R.G. requires the State's pleading to outline the facts and theory supporting a waiver of reunification efforts before the court may make that finding.
key_cases.quote: Moreover, any circumstances that increase the severity of the abuse or neglect, or add to its injurious consequences, equates to "aggravated circumstances."

timeline_requirements.deadline: Immediately upon receipt of the report; investigation initiated within 24 hours
timeline_requirements.starts_from: The Division's receipt of a report of child abuse or neglect
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Not specified in N.J.S.A. 9:6-8.11; a delay in initiating the investigation is permitted only where the Division or other designated entity authorizes it at the request of a law enforcement official.

timeline_requirements.starts_from: State Central Registry assigns the CPS report to the local office for response
timeline_requirements.consequence_of_miss: Good cause must be established and an extension approved by the local office manager or designee before day 60 (CP&P-II-C-6-200).
